name: UIGradient
simple: A UIGradient blends colors (and see-through-ness) smoothly across its parent UI object, like a sunset going from orange to purple. Put it inside a Frame, label, button or image. You can rotate it, slide it, and even fade part of the object out.
analogy: A UIGradient is like a colored filter you slide over a card. The filter goes from one color to another, and you can turn it at any angle.
whenToUse: Fancy backgrounds that fade between colors
Fading the edge of a panel to invisible
A 'shine' that sweeps across a button (animate Offset)
where: Put it inside a Frame, TextLabel, TextButton, ImageLabel, ImageButton, ViewportFrame or Path2D (or inside a UIStroke for gradient outlines). Not supported on ScrollingFrame or TextBox.

terms.modifier: A small invisible object you put INSIDE a UI object to change how it looks or behaves. It does nothing on its own.
terms.parent: The object something is placed inside. A modifier affects its parent.
terms.sibling: Objects that share the same parent, like brothers and sisters.
terms.UDim: Half of a UDim2: just one Scale and one Offset. UDim.new(0, 8) means 0% + 8 pixels. UDim.new(0.1, 0) means 10% of the parent's size.
terms.Scale: A fraction (0 to 1) of the parent's size. 0.5 = half.
terms.pixel: One tiny dot on the screen.
terms.LocalScript: A script that runs on the player's own device. UI code goes in LocalScripts.
terms.Vector2: Two numbers together: X (width or left-right) and Y (height or up-down).
terms.gradient: A smooth blend from one color to another.
terms.ColorSequence: A list of colors at points from 0 (start) to 1 (end). ColorSequence.new(red, blue) goes from red to blue.
terms.NumberSequence: A list of numbers at points from 0 to 1. For transparency, NumberSequence.new(0, 1) goes from solid to invisible.
terms.keypoint: One stop in a sequence: a position from 0 to 1 and a value (a color or a number).
terms.Color3: A color made of red, green and blue amounts.
terms.multiply: Mixing colors so white keeps the gradient color and black stays black. That's why gradients look best on white objects.
terms.tween: Smoothly animate a value from one number to another over time.

examples.title: A sunset background and a shine that sweeps across
examples.place: LocalScript inside a Frame (in a ScreenGui in StarterGui)
examples.code:
local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")
local frame = script.Parent
frame.BackgroundColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(255, 255, 255) -- white shows the gradient's true colors

local gradient = Instance.new("UIGradient")
gradient.Color = ColorSequence.new({
	ColorSequenceKeypoint.new(0, Color3.fromRGB(255, 140, 0)),  -- orange at the start
	ColorSequenceKeypoint.new(0.5, Color3.fromRGB(255, 60, 120)), -- pink in the middle
	ColorSequenceKeypoint.new(1, Color3.fromRGB(110, 40, 200)),   -- purple at the end
})
gradient.Rotation = 90 -- go top to bottom instead of left to right
gradient.Parent = frame

-- Slide the gradient from far up to far down, forever
gradient.Offset = Vector2.new(0, -1)
local tween = TweenService:Create(gradient, TweenInfo.new(3, Enum.EasingStyle.Linear, Enum.EasingDirection.InOut, -1, true), {Offset = Vector2.new(0, 1)})
tween:Play()
explain: The gradient is mixed with the frame's color, so we make the frame white to see the real colors.
ColorSequence has three stops: 0 = start, 0.5 = middle, 1 = end.
Rotation 90 turns the gradient so it runs from top to bottom.
Offset (0, -1) shifts the gradient up by one whole frame height; tweening to (0, 1) slides it down. -1 repeats forever and true makes it go back and forth.

gotchas: Gradient colors are mixed with the object's own color. On a black frame you'll see nothing; use white.
It doesn't affect children. Each child needs its own UIGradient.
Doesn't work on ScrollingFrame or TextBox.
Changing Color or Transparency often is slow. Animate Offset or Rotation instead.
Use 6 color stops or fewer for good performance.

UIGradient.Color.simple: The colors of the gradient, as a ColorSequence from start (0) to end (1). They're mixed with the parent's own color.
UIGradient.Color.example:
local gradient = script.Parent -- a UIGradient
gradient.Color = ColorSequence.new(Color3.fromRGB(0, 200, 255), Color3.fromRGB(0, 60, 160))

UIGradient.Enabled.simple: Turns the gradient on (true) or off (false) without deleting it.

UIGradient.Offset.simple: Slides the gradient, as a fraction of the parent's size. (1, 0) moves it right by one whole width; (0, 0.5) moves it down by half the height. On a 200-pixel-wide frame, Offset (0.25, 0) shifts it 50 pixels right. Animate it for a moving shine.

UIGradient.Rotation.simple: Turns the gradient clockwise by this many degrees. 0 (default) goes left to right, 90 goes top to bottom, 180 goes right to left.

UIGradient.Scale.simple: Stretches or squeezes the gradient. 1 (default) = the whole gradient fits once across the object. Under 1 squeezes it smaller (TileMode decides what fills the rest). Over 1 stretches it so only part shows.
UIGradient.Scale.example:
local gradient = script.Parent
gradient.Scale = 0.5
gradient.TileMode = Enum.GradientTileMode.Repeat -- repeat it twice across

UIGradient.TileMode.simple: What fills the leftover space when Scale is under 1 or Offset leaves a gap. For example, repeat the gradient, or mirror it.

UIGradient.Transparency.simple: How see-through the object is along the gradient, as a NumberSequence. 0 = solid, 1 = invisible. NumberSequence.new(0, 1) fades from solid to invisible.
UIGradient.Transparency.example:
local gradient = script.Parent
gradient.Transparency = NumberSequence.new(0, 1) -- fade out toward the end

UIGradient.Type.simple: The gradient's shape: Linear (straight bands, default), Radial (circles from the center), Elliptical (ovals), or Conical (sweeps around like a clock hand).
UIGradient.Type.example:
local gradient = script.Parent
gradient.Type = Enum.GradientType.Radial -- glow from the center
